title: Adjudicate announce from_bytes dispatch-prefix leniency: Rust-only vs C/Python stripped-only
description: Discovered by edge-cases codereview of worker6-b7z9.6 (announce length caps). Rust lichen-core Announce::from_bytes (announce.rs:88-95) accepts an optional leading L2_DISPATCH_ROUTING (0x15) byte and applies the 193-byte cap post-strip, so a raw 194-byte L2 routing payload (0x15 + 193-byte announce, the max legal on-air frame) parses. Python AnnounceMessage.from_bytes (python/src/lichen/announce/messages.py:118-124) and the C parse (lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/announce.c:253-261) take dispatch-stripped announce bytes only and would reject the same 194-byte input. No live caller misuses this today (Python/C callers strip before calling), but the leniency is Rust-only and unpinned by shared vectors (a 0x15-prefixed vector would fail the Python/C consumers by contract). Decide one contract: (a) document Rust strip as parser leniency (doc comment now says this) and pin with a Rust-only unit test, or (b) align Python/C to strip. Related context: worker6-balm tracks a similar C-vs-Python parse divergence.
